content:
Two senior military observers reported a sighting of a mysterious black triangular object that flew at an astonishing speed over a sensitive site in the western United States earlier this year. This revelation comes as part of a recent batch of UFO-related reports released by the Trump administration. The unidentified aerial phenomenon (UAP), a term favored by military and governmental entities in lieu of the traditional UFO designation, reportedly displayed none of the characteristics typical of conventional military aircraft.

In their assessment to the defense department, the observers noted that the object vanished suddenly and silently within seconds, leaving no trace, such as an exhaust trail. The precise location of the sighting was redacted in the publicly released file. The UAP resembled a delta-wing drone, measuring between 9 and 15 feet (approximately 2.75 to 4.5 meters) in wingspan, with a calculated speed of 1,800 mph.

This account adds to hundreds of similar reports issued by the Pentagon since May, contributing to an ongoing commitment by the Trump administration to enhance transparency regarding the government’s historical handling of UFO information. However, many details in these recent disclosures remain vague or obscured. Unlike previous sightings that often included photographic or video evidence, this particular report featured nine identical images of a canyon, with small triangular shapes crudely overlaid to depict the object’s movement.

Greg Eghigian, a professor and author, commented on the nature of the images, suggesting they do little to substantiate the claims made in the report. The Pentagon’s recent releases have become noticeably rarer in recent months, especially after President Trump announced in February his directive for full disclosure about government knowledge of UFOs and efforts to search for extraterrestrial life. This initiative followed serious allegations presented in Congress in 2023 by a former intelligence official, claiming that various administrations had concealed information regarding the existence of crashed alien spacecraft.

The latest release from the Pentagon contained fewer than 25 text documents, with no accompanying videos or images, marking a significant reduction in the volume of material made public in recent months. The ongoing mystery surrounding UAP sightings continues to fuel debates and speculation about unidentified aerial technologies and the implications of potential extraterrestrial life.
